statement: A general smooth complex cubic surface contains exactly 27 distinct projective lines.

source.location: Section VI, printed pages 258–260, with the cubic count on page 260
source.version: Original 1849 journal article, volume 4, pages 252–260, Internet Archive scan

scope: Lines on a general smooth complex cubic surface in projective three-space.
notes: Section VI computes the degree of the locus of points through which a line has fourth-order contact with a surface. For a cubic surface, such a line lies entirely on the surface. The cubic specialization gives degree 27 on printed page 260. This record uses the general smooth complex case of the classical calculation. Section V separately discusses singular cubic surfaces and the multiplicities assigned to their lines.
